title: Safe-area border and swipeable background should match and follow the theme
environment: Current updated phone build; Pixel 10 Pro XL running Android 17. Exact theme and row state at the time of the report are not yet recorded.
reproduction_status: Not independently reproduced during backlog gathering
reproduction_to_confirm: Open the shopping view and compare the safe-area border with the swipeable item background.
Switch between Light, Dark, and System themes and repeat the comparison.
Check unchecked and checked items, swipe feedback, and the keyboard-open layout.
actual: The user reports that the safe-area border and swipeable background do not have matching theme-following colors and instead appear to use an arbitrary color.
expected: The safe-area border matches the intended swipeable background surface, and both follow the selected theme coherently.
source_notes: View.qml defines safeAreaBackground.borderColor as the fixed translucent color #A6000000.
The active item surface in TextDelegate.qml uses Material.backgroundColor and opacity; checked rows intentionally use Theme.inverseTheme.
These are investigation starting points, not a confirmed root cause. The active row implementation is TextDelegate.qml rather than the unused legacy Swipeable.qml.
acceptance_criteria: Safe-area borders visually match the intended main swipeable background surface.
Colors update correctly when switching Light, Dark, and System themes.
Checked-state distinctions, swipe feedback, and the deliberate opacity design remain understandable.
Safe-area padding still keeps content clear of system bars and cutouts, including with the keyboard open.
Verify the appearance on the affected phone; model tests alone cannot establish this visual result.
open_questions: Which theme and item state best demonstrate the mismatch?
Confirm the intended shared surface when checked and unchecked rows deliberately use different theme colors.
evidence: User report in the QShopper development chat on 2026-10-28; severity explicitly described as minor.
